questions.q: Ad scheduling (ads only during certain hours) requires:
options: A daily budget with a spending cap per time slot
A lifetime budget to be able to schedule hours
A Bid Cap synchronized with the schedule
Reservation with delivery locked per hour
questions.explanation: Ad scheduling only exists with a lifetime budget: the system needs the period's total to distribute spend across the chosen slots.

options: Setting a manual, independent amount per ad set
Guaranteeing a fixed CPM throughout the whole campaign
Letting Meta distribute the budget across ad sets by opportunity
Scheduling spend by hours without a lifetime budget
questions.explanation: CBO puts the budget at campaign level and the system moves it toward the ad sets with the best opportunity. Manual amounts per ad set is ABO.

options: Expected impressions × historical CPM ÷ 1,000
Target results × expected cost per result
Committed reach × promised frequency × fixed CPM
Last year's budget + estimated inflation
questions.explanation: In Auction you plan from the result: how many you need × what each one costs. The reach × frequency × CPM formula belongs to Reservation.

questions.q: Reservation plan: 400,000 people, frequency 2, fixed CPM $5. Approximate budget:
options: $2,000 — you pay only for unique people, not per impression
$8,000 — each frequency is bought separately at double
$40,000 — the CPM applies per 100 impressions
questions.explanation: Impressions = 400,000 × 2 = 800,000. Divided by 1,000 = 800 thousands × $5 = $4,000. CPM is always cost per THOUSAND impressions.

questions.q: Main risk of a budget that's too low in Auction:
options: The ad gets rejected in the ad review process for insufficient spend
Meta converts the campaign to Reservation automatically
The bid strategy resets to Highest Volume without notice
The ad set never exits the learning phase and performance stays unstable
questions.explanation: Without ~50 optimization events per week, the ad set keeps learning: volatile costs and unstable results. Review doesn't look at your budget.

questions.q: A campaign with 6 ad sets, no time to adjust splits by hand and uneven performance across audiences:
options: ABO with equal amounts per ad set for a clean audience comparison
CBO: the system moves spend toward the ad sets with the best opportunity
Lifetime budget with Monday-to-Friday ad scheduling
Reservation to guarantee the split among the six
questions.explanation: Many ad sets + zero management time + uneven performance = CBO. ABO is for when you NEED guaranteed spend per audience (e.g. tests).

questions.q: When is ABO (budget per ad set) better than CBO?
options: When you need guaranteed minimum spend per audience (e.g. controlled tests)
When you prefer the system to optimize the spend split for you on its own
When the budget is lifetime and ad scheduling is active
When the campaign is Reservation with a locked CPM
questions.explanation: ABO gives control: each ad set spends what you assign, ideal for tests or market quotas. CBO optimizes better when you don't need that control.

questions.q: You need ~400 leads this month and your historical CPL is ~$5 USD. Base budget:
options: $800 USD: half, because optimization makes the rest cheaper
$4,000 USD: double, to cover the full learning phase
$2,000 USD: 400 leads × $5 expected cost per lead
$5,000 USD: a thousand per week plus a safety margin
questions.explanation: Target results × expected cost = 400 × $5 = $2,000. It's the base; you adjust with real data later, but you never start by guessing.

questions.q: Learning phase: what resets it and why does it matter?
options: Only pausing the campaign for more than 24 hours restarts it
Significant edits (audience, creative, bid) restart learning and destabilize cost
Renaming the ad set restarts the learning phase
Nothing resets it: it lasts exactly 7 days regardless of any edits you make
questions.explanation: Significant edits send the ad set back to learning: that's why edits are batched and the campaign isn't poked daily.

options: Daily allows ad scheduling; lifetime forces uniform spend
Daily is only available in Auction campaigns; lifetime is exclusive to campaigns bought via Reservation
Daily spends ~the amount each day; lifetime spreads a total across the period and allows ad scheduling
Daily requires CBO enabled; lifetime requires ABO
questions.explanation: Daily = approximate daily pace. Lifetime = a period total with flexible distribution, and it's the only one that enables ad scheduling.
